blocks.prompt: 3 (i) [printed as 2 (i)] Find the linear approximation of the following functions at the given points: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x^{2} + 16}\) at \(x = 3\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh \(x = 3\) par linearization hai.
Diya kya hai? \(f(x) = \sqrt{x^{2} + 16}\). Find kya karna hai? \(L(x)\).
Centre 3 kyun acha hai? Kyun ke \(3^{2} + 16 = 25\) perfect square hai, values bilkul saaf niklengi.
Plan: \(f(3)\), chain rule se \(f'(x)\), phir \(f'(3)\) aur \(L(x)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x^{2} + 16}\), centre \(a = 3\).
Maloom karna: \(L(x)\).
Tareeqa: \(L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)\).

Centre par value
\[f(3) = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5\]
Kyun: tangent line point \((3, 5)\) se guzregi.

Derivative
\[f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x^{2} + 16}} \cdot 2x\]
\[= \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 16}}\]
\[f'(3) = \dfrac{3}{5}\]
Kyun: chain rule: bahar square root ka derivative \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\), aur andar \(x^{2} + 16\) ka derivative \(2x\). 2 cancel ho gaya.
Dhyan dein: andar ka \(2x\) bhool jana sab se aam ghalti hai.

Tasdeeq \(x = 3.1\) par
\[L(3.1) = \dfrac{25.3}{5} = 5.06\]
\[f(3.1) = \sqrt{25.61} = 5.06063\]
Bohat qareeb, yani linearization sahi hai.

blocks.text: Kitab mein sawal number 2 do dafa chhapa hai (1, 2, 2, 3). Yeh doosra "2" yahan Question 3 hai, aur us ke baad wala "3" Question 4 hai. Is ke parts (i), (ii), (ii) chhape hain; aakhri part (\(f(x) = \cos x\) at \(x = 0\)) asal mein (iii) hona chahiye.
blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti

blocks.prompt: 3 (ii) [printed as 2 (ii)] Find the linear approximation of the following functions at the given points: \(f(x) = \tan x\) at \(x = \pi\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh \(x = \pi\) par linearization hai.
Diya kya hai? \(f(x) = \tan x\). Find kya karna hai? \(L(x)\).
\(\pi\) par \(\tan \pi = 0\) aur \(\cos \pi = -1\) maloom hain, is liye hisaab aasaan hai.
Plan: \(f(\pi)\), \(f'(\pi)\), phir \(L(x)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \tan x\), centre \(a = \pi\).
Maloom karna: \(L(x)\).
Tareeqa: \(L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)\).

Derivative
\[f'(x) = \sec^{2} x\]
\[f'(\pi) = \dfrac{1}{\cos^{2}\pi} = \dfrac{1}{(-1)^{2}} = 1\]
Kyun: \(\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}\) aur \(\cos \pi = -1\). Square karne se minus khatam ho jata hai, is liye slope 1.

Linearization
\[L(x) = 0 + 1(x - \pi) = x - \pi\]
Kyun: values formula mein rakhin; seedhi si line mil gayi.
blocks.final_answer: \(L(x) = x - \pi\), yani \(x = \pi\) ke qareeb \(\tan x \approx x - \pi\).

blocks.prompt: 3 (iii) [printed as 2 (ii)] Find the linear approximation of the following functions at the given points: \(f(x) = \cos x\) at \(x = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh \(x = 0\) par linearization hai.
Diya kya hai? \(f(x) = \cos x\). Find kya karna hai? \(L(x)\).
Is sawal ki khaas baat: yahan slope zero niklega, to line bilkul flat (horizontal) hogi.
Plan: \(f(0)\), \(f'(0)\), phir \(L(x)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \cos x\), centre \(a = 0\).
Maloom karna: \(L(x)\).
Tareeqa: \(L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)\).

Centre par value aur slope
\[f(0) = \cos 0 = 1\]
\[f'(x) = -\sin x,\ f'(0) = 0\]
Kyun: \(\sin 0 = 0\), is liye slope zero.

Linearization
\[L(x) = 1 + 0(x - 0) = 1\]
Kyun: \((0, 1)\) cosine curve ki choti (sab se ooncha point) hai, wahan tangent horizontal hota hai. Is liye linear approximation sirf constant 1 hai. Yeh bhi bilkul jaiz linear approximation hai.
